claims.claim: Railway estimates unauthorized spend on the stolen keys at about $740,000.
claims.quote: Unauthorized spend on the stolen keys was estimated to reach ~$740,000.

claims.claim: at most 1.85% (about 100,000) of workspaces could have had variables decrypted
claims.quote: obtain and decrypt a subset of customer variables, for at most, 1.85% (~100,000) of workspaces

claims.claim: used a previously unknown flaw in its build infrastructure to get out of isolation on 20 October, then decrypted variables, 'prioritizing AI provider keys'
claims.quote: At 07:28 UTC on October 20th the attacker exploited a previously unknown vulnerability ... partially escape filesystem isolation; the attacker was specifically prioritizing AI provider keys in their queries
claims.fix: Isolation escape was a 'partial' filesystem-isolation escape. The page says 'prioritizing AI provider keys in their queries' (brief's quoted words are a fragment, fine).

claims.claim: Stolen keys got spent in hours (opening line)
claims.quote: Searched whole page for 'hours': the word does not appear; no interval between theft and spend is given. Only 'The unauthorized usage we have observed since ranges from coding agents to AI training pipelines.'
claims.fix: Drop 'in hours'; say 'Stolen keys were used for about $740,000 of unauthorized spend'.

claims.claim: Fixed in: Railway says all exploited vulnerabilities are remediated and builds now run on ephemeral VMs
claims.quote: Each of the attack vectors used during the incident has been remediated. ... Each build now gets a dedicated ephemeral virtual machine
claims.fix: Say 'each of the attack vectors used has been remediated' (report calls its improvement list 'by no means an exhaustive list'); ephemeral-VM claim is correct.

claims.claim: Fixed in: no versions stated; Severity: not stated in the report
claims.quote: Searched whole page for 'severity', 'CVE', versions: 'severity' and 'CVE' do not appear; no software versions. 'critical' appears only as 'customers with critical workloads' and 'in critical areas'.

claims.claim: Stopgap: rotate credentials stored on Railway, especially AI provider keys
claims.quote: When possible, we suggested that customers attempt credential rotation manually via SSH.
claims.fix: Report never explicitly tells customers to rotate AI provider keys; it says Railway suggested credential rotation and advised high-risk customers to turn off deployments. Present rotation (esp. AI keys) as the brief's own advice, not Railway's.

claims.claim: If compromised: report charges you didn't make via the form in the report
claims.quote: report charges that they didn't make (linked Google form)

claims.claim: If compromised: redeploy the latest commit and reconnect GitHub
claims.quote: Only in a sidebar teaser for a different post: 'Redeploy the latest commit, reconnect GitHub, and recreate CLI and CI credentials to get your services deploying again.'
claims.fix: Not part of the report body; remove or cite the separate Railway post. 'Rotate everything' is also not stated.

claims.claim: BleepingComputer: ~$740,000 in fraudulent AI charges
claims.quote: The stolen credentials were subsequently used to generate approximately $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage.

claims.claim: Gemini 4 Carbon goes GA (headline) / out of limited release
claims.quote: Today, we're making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. (Searched page for 'generally available', 'general availability', 'GA', 'limited': none appear)
claims.fix: Google says 'now available' via API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business 'for all paying developers and enterprises'; it never says GA. Headline should say 'is now available' not 'goes GA'.

claims.claim: after a first release to cyber defenders about two weeks earlier
claims.quote: Two weeks ago, we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders.

claims.claim: $2/$10 per million tokens introductory, rising to $4/$20 after 30 November
claims.quote: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens ... the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply after November 30, 2026
claims.fix: Access is 'for all paying developers and enterprises'.

claims.claim: ranks first on CursorBench 4.0 at more than 2X lower cost per task than the next best external model
claims.quote: ranks #1 ... at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model
claims.fix: Vendor benchmark, as the brief says.

claims.claim: attack breach rate fell from 3.1% on Gemini 4 Argon to 0.8%
claims.quote: lowered the per-attempt breach rate to just 0.8% (down from 3.1% on Argon)

claims.claim: Teleport made Beams generally available on 9 November
claims.quote: Teleport Beams is generally available as of November 9, 2026 (dateline: OAKLAND, CA - November 10, 2026)
claims.fix: Press release is dated 10 November; GA as of 9 November.

claims.claim: ephemeral micro-VM with traffic captured; secretless access to cloud accounts, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL and MCP servers
claims.quote: ephemeral micro-VMs ... captures all protocol traffic in the audit record ... no secrets or passwords in the agent's environment

claims.claim: no standing privileges until a human or an LLM judge approves its execution plan; global kill switch
claims.quote: zero standing privileges ... A human or an LLM judge reviews and revises each plan.
claims.fix: Source says the judge 'reviews and revises' each plan; 'approves' is the brief's wording. Kill switch: teams can halt all agent activity at once (not literally named 'global').

items.vendor_cap_exception: Research disclosure on model provenance; Microsoft was a main item on 9 Nov

claims.claim: rewriting fewer than 10 dormant neurons, with no retraining, is enough to backdoor any agent built on it
claims.quote: weight-reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM, is enough to backdoor an agent built on it. These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model.
claims.fix: Source says 'an agent built on it', not 'any agent'. Research claim; page does not say peer-reviewed or independently verified.

claims.claim: passes standard evaluations until a trigger such as a date change
claims.quote: still passing standard safety evaluations ... The trigger can be as mundane as a date change.

claims.claim: Reliable detection needs the original, unmodified weights
claims.quote: Reliable detection requires diff'ing against the original, unmodified weights.

claims.claim: Microsoft says signed models and weight scanning are planned, not shipped
claims.quote: Also being planned is having models be signed with verifiable provenance and tamper-proof audits.
claims.fix: Page separately describes 'AI-powered weight scanning' as a planned defense.

claims.claim: open-source checkpoint and restore tool for GPU workloads on Kubernetes
claims.quote: open-source checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes
claims.fix: Blog states no licence terms; brief gives none.

claims.claim: On B200 GPUs it restored models in 3.6 to 42.7 seconds, 8 to 36 times faster than a cold start
claims.quote: 3.6 to 42.7 seconds ... roughly 8x to 36x faster than cold starts

claims.claim: the largest MoE models take 6 to 19 minutes cold; tested on vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM
claims.quote: cold starts of "6 to 19 minutes" (MoE models with checkpoints up to 1 TB across eight GPUs); engines: vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT LLM

claims.claim: Restores need the same GPU model and driver as the checkpoint
claims.quote: Restores must run on a node with the same GPU model and driver.
